chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the faith of God’s elect and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness, VerseEnd Verse2 in hope of eternal life — which God (who cannot lie) promised before the world began, VerseEnd Verse3 but has in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Savior VerseEnd — Verse4 to Titus, my own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior. VerseEnd

Verse5 For this cause I left you in Crete: that you should set in order the things that are lacking, and ordain elders in every city as I had appointed you VerseEnd — Verse6 if any are blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly. VerseEnd Verse7 For a bishop must be blameless as the steward of God, not self-willed, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy money, VerseEnd Verse8 but a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate, VerseEnd Verse9 holding fast the faithful word as he has been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to refute the opponents; VerseEnd Verse10 for there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers — especially they of the circumcision VerseEnd — Verse11 whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not for filthy money’s sake. VerseEnd Verse12 One of them, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle gluttons. VerseEnd Verse13 This witness is true. Wherefore, rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith, VerseEnd Verse14 not giving heed to Jewish fables and commandments of men that turn from the truth. VerseEnd Verse15 Unto the pure, let all things be pure, but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure, but even their mind and conscience is defiled. VerseEnd Verse16 They profess that they know God, but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 But speak the things which become sound doctrine VerseEnd — Verse2 that the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience; VerseEnd Verse3 the aged women likewise, that they be in behavior as becomes holiness: not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things, VerseEnd Verse4 that they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, VerseEnd Verse5 to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed. VerseEnd Verse6 Young men likewise exhort to be sober-minded, VerseEnd Verse7 in all things showing yourself a pattern of good works, in doctrine showing incorruptness, gravity, sincerity, VerseEnd Verse8 sound speech that cannot be condemned — that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. VerseEnd Verse9 Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things, VerseEnd Verse10 not answering again, not stealing, but showing all good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior in all things. VerseEnd Verse11 For the grace of God which brings salvation to all men has appeared, VerseEnd Verse12 teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world, VerseEnd Verse13 looking for that blessed hope and the glorious appearing of the great God, and our Savior Jesus Christ VerseEnd Verse14 who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify unto himself a peculiar people zealous of good works. VerseEnd Verse15 These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise you. VerseEnd LEChapter3 Verse1 Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, VerseEnd Verse2 to speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, showing all meekness unto all men. VerseEnd

Verse3 For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving diverse lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. VerseEnd Verse4 But after that, the kindness and love of God our Savior toward man appeared VerseEnd — Verse5 not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy. He saved us by the washing of regeneration and renewing of the holy ghost, VerseEnd Verse6 which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior, VerseEnd Verse7 that being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. VerseEnd Verse8 This is a faithful saying, and these things I desire that you affirm constantly, that they who have believed in God might be anxious to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men. VerseEnd Verse9 But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law, for they are unprofitable and vain. VerseEnd Verse10 A man that is a heretic after the first and second admonition reject, VerseEnd Verse11 knowing that he who is such is subverted and sins, being condemned of himself. VerseEnd

Verse12 When I shall send Artemas unto you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis, for I have determined there to winter. VerseEnd Verse13 Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be lacking unto them, VerseEnd Verse14 and let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful. VerseEnd Verse15 All that are with me salute you. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The epistle written to Titus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Cretans, from Nicopolis of Macedonia.
